name: Langfuse
tagline: An LLM engineering platform for developing, monitoring, evaluating, and debugging AI applications.
hook: A contributor guide to monorepo dependencies, seed data, stale builds, handoff evidence, public explanations, and agent config.
summary: Langfuse keeps its canonical guide at .agents/AGENTS.md and gives outside contributors different context from maintainers. It covers monorepo dependencies, reproducible seed data, proof in handoffs, public explanations, and agent configuration generated from one source.

techniques.title: Distinguish cached success from fresh execution
techniques.body: The verification section explains that Turbo prints a successful task count for both cache hits and executed tasks. It requires the cached count as evidence and names the force option for a fresh run.
techniques.quote: A check that passed is not always a check that ran:

techniques.title: Keep test data reproducible through named scenarios
techniques.body: Local test state goes through the seed CLI. When a bug needs a new data shape, the guide asks whether it belongs in a reusable seeder scenario instead of a one-off database edit.
techniques.quote:
Prefill local test data with the seed CLI (`pnpm run seed -- list` shows
  scenarios; runs print UI deep links) — never with ad-hoc scripts or raw
  ClickHouse inserts.

techniques.title: Give outside contributors a smaller context boundary
techniques.body: The opening limits outside-contributor work to code and contribution guidance. Tracker state and handbook context are reserved for maintainers, so participation does not depend on internal organizational access.
techniques.quote:
**Outside contributor** → code and `CONTRIBUTING.md` only (build, checks, PRs).
No tracker, handbook, or working-week context.

techniques.title: Explain why a production bundle needs its own check
techniques.body: The guide names minifier-dropped bindings and Node globals leaking into browser chunks as runtime failures that development builds and type checks miss. It points to the production bundle scanner and its documented fix.
techniques.quote:
the SWC dropped-binding class ships
  runtime-only `ReferenceError`s that dev builds and type checks cannot see.

techniques.title: Keep public explanations independent of internal tickets
techniques.body: The guide prohibits ticket IDs and tracker URLs in code comments, commit messages, PR text, and user docs. It explains that those identifiers have no meaning for outside readers and limits a provenance exception to maintainer skill files.
techniques.quote:
Describe the problem on its own terms; a ticket-prefixed
  branch name is the one place the identifier belongs.

techniques.title: Generate tool-specific guidance from a canonical source
techniques.body: The .agents guide is the root source, with AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md symlinks and synchronization commands. Package-local instructions live in their narrowest owning directory, while provider shims remain generated artifacts.
techniques.quote:
Put package-local guidance in the narrowest `AGENTS.md` that owns it so that it's only
  loaded into context when needed.

steal: Report whether verification executed or reused a cache.
Turn bug-specific test data into reusable seed scenarios.
Separate contributor context from maintainer-only context.
Name failures that type checking cannot detect.
Write public explanations without internal ticket dependencies.
Generate tool compatibility files from canonical instructions.
